headline: NAB's cash earnings fell $11 million (0.2%) to $7,091 million in FY25 from $7,102 million in FY24, remaining broadly stable. Statutory net profit from continuing operations fell $275 million to $6,788 million (from $7,063 million), with $303 million of non-cash items (hedging/fair value, amortisation, acquisition/disposal costs) separating it from cash earnings. Underlying profit rose $142 million (1.3%) to $10,965 million, supported by $577 million of revenue growth (NII +$644m, partly offset by OOI -$67m) and $435 million of higher operating expenses (including $130m payroll review/remediation). Credit impairment charges rose $105 million to $833 million, and tax expense increased $27 million to $3,002 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $644 million (3.8%) to $17,398 million, driven by volume growth (average IEA up $22.5 billion or 2.3%) and a 3 bps NIM improvement to 1.74%, partially offset by a $74 million hedge movement included in NII but excluded from underlying. Excluding hedges, underlying NII rose $718 million (4.3%).

Other operating income fell $67 million (1.9%) to $3,415 million, partially offset by the $74 million hedge decrease in NII. Revenue excluding M&T rose only 1.4%, impacted by higher customer-related remediation charges ($102 million in FY25 vs $35 million in FY24) and business disposals/run-offs.

Underlying operating expenses increased $435 million (4.6%) to $9,848 million. Excluding $130 million of payroll review and remediation costs, underlying opex rose $305 million (3.2%), driven by $271 million higher personnel expenses (salary inflation, investment in bankers) and $71 million higher technology expenses, partially offset by productivity benefits of $420 million.

Payroll review and remediation costs of $130 million were incurred in FY25 ($101 million in personnel expenses, $29 million in general expenses), compared to nil in FY24. These are disclosed separately from underlying operating expenses.

Credit impairment charge rose $105 million (14.4%) to $833 million. Individually assessed charges increased $328 million to $964 million (C&IB impairments, non-recurrence of FY24 write-backs/recoveries, modest increases in B&PB/NZ/retail). Collective provisions swung from a $92 million charge to a $131 million write-back ($223 million improvement), driven by forward-looking provision releases.

Income tax expense increased $27 million (0.9%) to $3,002 million, due to higher pre-tax earnings and a 10 bps rise in the effective tax rate to 29.6% (mainly lower deferred tax asset for US tax losses). Non-controlling interests widened by $21 million to $39 million.

Cash earnings were broadly stable over the year. While credit impairment charges increased, pleasingly a number of key asset quality outcomes improved over 2H25

Revenue increased by 2.9% with key drivers including volume growth and higher Markets & Treasury (M&T) income, partially offset by higher customer-related remediation charges and the impact from business disposals and run-offs. Excluding M&T income, revenue rose 1.4% over the year

Expenses increased by 4.6% including $130 million related to payroll review and remediation charges. Excluding payroll review and remediation charges, expenses rose 3.2% reflecting higher personnel and technology related costs, partially offset by productivity benefits and lower costs relating to the Group's Enforceable Undertaking with AUSTRAC.

Credit impairment charge was $833 million, versus a FY24 charge of $728 million. The FY25 charge includes individually assessed charges of $964 million and a $131 million release from collective provisions.

Net interest income increased by $644 million or 3.8%. This includes a decrease of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in other operating income. Excluding this movement, the underlying increase of $718 million or 4.3% was due to higher average interest earning assets and net interest margin.
Net interest income increased by $644 million or 3.8%. This includes a decrease of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in other operating income.
Operating expenses increased by $435 million or 4.6%. Excluding an increase of $130 million for payroll review and remediation costs, operating expenses increased by $305 million or 3.2%.

Personnel expenses increased by $271 million or 4.8%. Excluding an increase of $101 million for payroll review and remediation costs, personnel expenses increased by $170 million or 3.0%. The increase was driven by salary expense inflation, investment in additional bankers and resources to support growth, and continued investment in technology and financial crime related capabilities.

Credit impairment charge increased by $105 million or 14.4% to $833 million, driven by a higher level of individually assessed credit impairment charge primarily in Corporate and Institutional Banking. This was partially offset by a lower level of collective credit impairment charge.
Collective credit impairment charge decreased by $223 million from a charge of $92 million to a write-back of $131 million.

Credit impairment charge increased by $105 million or 14.4% to $833 million, driven by a higher level of individually assessed credit impairment charge primarily in Corporate and Institutional Banking.
Income tax expense increased by $27 million or 0.9% due to higher cash earnings before income tax and a higher effective tax rate.
The effective tax rate increased by 10 basis points to 29.6% primarily due to a decrease in the amount recognised as a deferred tax asset for U.S. tax losses.
In the September 2025 full year, there was an increase in statutory profit of $39 million ($28 million after tax) from hedging and fair value volatility.
In the September 2025 full year, there was a decrease in statutory profit of $49 million ($36 million after tax) due to the amortisation of acquired intangible assets.
